CORAL

COntextual Reasoning And Local Planning in A Hierarchical VLM Framework for Underwater Monitoring

Zhenqi Wu* ·  Yuanjie Lu† ·  Xuesu Xiao† ·  Xiaomin Lin*

* University of South Florida   † George Mason University

📄 arXiv 💻 Code Coming Soon 🎥 Video
Abstract

Decoupling Semantic Reasoning from Reactive Control

Oyster reefs sustain biodiversity, filter water, and protect coastlines, yet 85% have been lost globally. Restoring these ecosystems requires regular underwater monitoring — a task that remains costly and hazardous for human divers. Autonomous underwater vehicles offer a promising alternative, but existing systems rely on geometry-based navigation that cannot interpret scene semantics. Recent vision-language models enable semantic reasoning, yet existing VLM-driven systems adopt an end-to-end paradigm, introducing three key limitations: frequent inference delays, collision risk from dynamics blindness, and accumulating path errors from limited self-correction.


We propose CORAL, a hierarchical framework that decouples high-level semantic reasoning from low-level reactive control. The VLM provides exploration guidance by selecting waypoints from a structured centroid chain; a dynamics-based planner handles collision-free execution; and a geometric verification module closes the self-correction loop. CORAL improves coverage by 14.28 pp, reduces collisions by 100%, and requires 57% fewer VLM calls compared with the prior state-of-the-art.

Method

Hierarchical Architecture Overview

CORAL separates the navigation stack into three tightly integrated layers: a persistent occupancy map with centroid chain extraction, a VLM high-level planner invoked only at meaningful decision points, and a dynamics-aware MDDP low-level controller running continuously at 10 Hz.

Fig. 2 — Overview of the CORAL framework. Dashed lines indicate VLM-triggered flows; solid lines indicate constant information flow.
🗺️
Perception & Centroid Chain
Depth and segmentation images are fused into a persistent 2D occupancy map. Oyster cluster centroids are extracted via connected component analysis and organized into an ordered chain using a nearest-neighbor greedy algorithm with cross-frame exponential smoothing.
🧠
VLM High-Level Planner
A smart trigger invokes the VLM only on goal arrival, stuck detection, or planner failure. The VLM selects centroid indices for compact clusters or predicts free waypoints for elongated reefs. A geometric verifier rejects backward or off-trend waypoints with structured corrective feedback.
⚙️
MDDP Low-Level Controller
MDDP augments MPPI with variable-fidelity dynamics: dense collision checking and high-accuracy dynamics near the robot, progressively simplified further along the rollout, enabling long-horizon planning through narrow reef passages at zero collisions.
Simulation

Simulation Environments

10 Blender environments across 5 reef topology classes — from basic turning layouts to closed loops and multi-prong dead ends — with randomized oyster densities and dense obstacle placements.

Real-World Deployment

Pool Trials — BlueROV2

CORAL deployed on a BlueROV2 Heavy in a controlled pool (12 ft diameter, 5 ft depth) with oyster shells and floating ball obstacles. Perception runs on-board in real time; VLM queries reach cloud API endpoints asynchronously.
